rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan-review store `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` hides the record shape, version/blob path resolution, the content fingerprint, response tracking and report delivery behind a small public API (`plan_fingerprint`, `store_plan_review`, `read_plan_review`, `list_plan_reviews`, `record_response`, `declined_recurrence`), and the dispatch composer in `reckon/crew/recovery.py:_review_dispatch_fields` hides both review subjects — a run and a plan — behind one function rather than a second composer.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the shared infrastructure at risk of forking is the review store root, and the plan reuses it: `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:295,399,480` resolve through `reckon.crew.review.review_store_root`, so plan reviews and code reviews share one root and one namespace (`plan-<slug>.v<N>.json` beside `<run_id>.json`). The plan-review reader in `plan_review.py` (`_candidate_paths`, `read_plan_review`, `list_plan_reviews`) serves a genuinely different key — plan slug, version and content fingerprint — than the owner `reckon/crew/review.py:read_review`/`stored_record`, which key on reviewed run id and head revision; it is new keying, not a second copy of `review.py`'s index/partial-record machinery (which is not duplicated), so no shared mechanism is forked.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §3 extends two mechanisms it names and the code confirms both: the build skill's manual prior-art-scout reuse-map (`skills/reckon-build/references/coordinator-reference.md` §1b), and `reckon/interface_counts.py`, whose docstring states it counts "the ones the plan-review rubric reads" and whose `count_revision_cached` is the same reader `reckon/velocity.py:2513` already consumes.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the design extends the shared review reflex rather than wrapping it: `_review_dispatch_fields` gains a `subject == "plan"` branch (recovery.py:521) and `plan_review_subject` (recovery.py:438) is a thin adapter that feeds the existing composer, so the plan review reuses the run-review path; §7's `plan_review_settle_seconds` is a declared config key read through the existing flight resolver, not a wrapper over new machinery.
